draft.title: p-values and significance
card: The p-value is the probability of a sample result at least as extreme as the one observed, if H₀ is true.
The significance level, α, is chosen before the test. A common choice is 0.05.
If p < α, reject H₀. There is evidence for H₁. If p > α, do not reject H₀. The evidence is not strong enough.
Example: with α = 0.05, a p-value of 0.03 gives evidence to reject H₀. A p-value of 0.20 does not.
draft.remember: A p-value below the significance level is evidence to reject H₀.

a.q: A test has α = 0.05 and gives a p-value of 0.02. What is the conclusion?
opts: Reject H₀, as 0.02 is less than 0.05
Do not reject H₀, as 0.02 is a small value
Reject H₁, as 0.02 is less than 0.05
Do not reject H₀, as 0.02 is not equal to 0.05
a.why: The p-value 0.02 is below α = 0.05, so there is evidence to reject H₀. A small p-value is a reason to reject H₀, not to keep it.
a.clue: Compare the p-value with α. Which is smaller?

b.q: Sam tests a new fertiliser at α = 0.01 and gets p = 0.03. What is the correct conclusion?
opts: Do not reject H₀, as 0.03 is greater than 0.01
Reject H₀, as 0.03 is less than 0.05
Reject H₀, as 0.03 is a small probability
Do not reject H₀, as 0.03 is less than 0.05
b.why: The level here is 0.01, not 0.05. Since 0.03 is above 0.01, the evidence is not strong enough to reject H₀. Using 0.05 would give the wrong conclusion.
b.clue: Use the α given in the question, not the usual one.

a.best: Reject H₀, as 0.02 is less than 0.05

b.best: Do not reject H₀, as 0.03 is greater than 0.01

final.title: p-values and significance
card: The p-value is the probability of a sample result at least as extreme as the one observed, if \(H_{0}\) is true.
The significance level, \(\alpha\), is chosen before the test. A common choice is 0.05.
If \(p < \alpha\), reject \(H_{0}\). There is evidence for \(H_{1}\). If \(p > \alpha\), do not reject \(H_{0}\). The evidence is not strong enough.
Example: with \(\alpha = 0.05\), a p-value of 0.03 gives evidence to reject \(H_{0}\). A p-value of 0.20 does not.
final.remember: A p-value below the significance level is evidence to reject \(H_{0}\).

a.q: A test has \(\alpha = 0.05\) and gives a p-value of 0.02. What is the conclusion?
opts: Reject \(H_{0}\), as 0.02 is less than 0.05
Do not reject \(H_{0}\), as 0.02 is a small value
Reject \(H_{1}\), as 0.02 is less than 0.05
Do not reject \(H_{0}\), as 0.02 is not equal to 0.05
a.why: The p-value 0.02 is below \(\alpha = 0.05\), so there is evidence to reject \(H_{0}\). A small p-value is a reason to reject \(H_{0}\), not to keep it.
a.clue: Compare the p-value with \(\alpha\). Which is smaller?

b.q: Sam tests a new fertiliser at \(\alpha = 0.01\) and gets \(p = 0.03\). What is the correct conclusion?
opts: Do not reject \(H_{0}\), as 0.03 is greater than 0.01
Reject \(H_{0}\), as 0.03 is less than 0.05
Reject \(H_{0}\), as 0.03 is a small probability
Do not reject \(H_{0}\), as 0.03 is less than 0.05
b.why: The level here is 0.01, not 0.05. Since 0.03 is above 0.01, the evidence is not strong enough to reject \(H_{0}\). Using 0.05 would give the wrong conclusion.
b.clue: Use the \(\alpha\) given in the question, not the usual one.
